title: San Francisco Office Space Guide
meta_description: A practical guide to finding office space in San Francisco, including average rents, leasing trends, neighborhood notes, and nearby office markets.
rent_basis: Annual full-service/gross asking rent, based on Q1 2026 market reports.
summary: San Francisco’s office market is showing signs of renewed demand, led by AI, technology, and companies seeking high-quality, move-in-ready space. Vacancy remains elevated, but leasing activity has improved and tenants have more options than they did during the pre-2020 peak.
trends: AI and technology tenants are driving much of the strongest leasing demand.
Move-in-ready and amenity-rich buildings are outperforming older commodity office space.
Smaller tenants still have leverage, especially when comparing traditional offices, sublease space, and flexible office options.
The strongest activity is concentrated in prime downtown and transit-accessible submarkets.

neighborhoods.name: Financial District
neighborhoods.summary: Best for professional services, finance, legal, consulting, and companies that value BART, ferry, and Muni access.

neighborhoods.name: SoMa
neighborhoods.summary: Popular with technology, design, startup, and creative companies looking for loft-style buildings, larger floor plates, and proximity to Caltrain.

neighborhoods.name: Mission Bay
neighborhoods.summary: A strong fit for life science, biotech, healthcare, and growing technology companies near UCSF and newer mixed-use development.

neighborhoods.name: Jackson Square / North Beach
neighborhoods.summary: Good for boutique firms, creative companies, and teams that want a more distinctive neighborhood feel.

neighborhoods.name: Mid-Market
neighborhoods.summary: Offers value and central transit access, with renewed interest from arts, culture, startup, and adaptive reuse activity.
